heuristics.statement: For the fixed map F(v) = SHA3-256-r7(enc(v)), enc(v) = the 135-byte constant K of proof Section 1 with the four 64-bit words of v written into lanes 0, 1, 2, 4 and 10, 11, 12, 14, walks from fresh uniform start words behave, for the events used in the success bound, as walks of a uniformly random function on {0,1}^256: F at a point not evaluated before is a fresh uniform 256-bit value independent of all values observed so far.
heuristics.scope: Success probability only (first-repeat time, iid distinguished-point coins giving geometric trail positions and lockstep detection delay, binomial count of distinguished points, start hit rates), r = 7, about 2^128 evaluations. Output correctness and the enforced op budget do not depend on it.
heuristics.extrapolation: No experiment at 2^128 scale; the algorithm's success model is checked by a scaled simulation under the random-function model (proof Section 8). Sensitivity: repeats at kappa times the random rate keep the bound >= 0.39 for kappa >= 0.9984; otherwise time_log2 rises by about (1/2) log2(1/kappa).
heuristics.limitations: F is not random; no proof that F on this encoding is not closer to injective than a random function. For r <= 2 the heuristic is not credible.
